\label{sec:70b-results}

-On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (AWQ INT4), zero-shot S1 eliminates DR on both datasets: SciERC 6.41\%\,$\to$\,0\% (R-F1 11.24, $+$0.09\,pp), DocRED 14.98\%\,$\to$\,0\% (R-F1 13.05, $+$0.04\,pp); CF rises to 3.50--7.01\% (from $\leq$0.07\%), comparable to 8B zero-shot CF.

+On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (AWQ INT4), zero-shot S1 eliminates DR on both datasets: SciERC 6.41\%\,$\to$\,0\% (R-F1 11.24), DocRED 14.98\%\,$\to$\,0\% (R-F1 13.05); CF rises to 3.50--7.01\%, comparable to 8B zero-shot CF.
% TODO: 待 70B LoRA DocRED 200-doc + CF 数据回填

LoRA fine-tuning confirms scale-independent composability: SciERC DR 1.50\%\,$\to$\,0\% (R-F1 44.53, $-$0.20\,pp); DocRED (200-document subset) DR XX.XX\%\,$\to$\,XX.XX\% (R-F1 XX.XX); CF drops from 3.50\% (zero-shot) to 1.33\% (LoRA), consistent with the 8B pattern (9.90\%\,$\to$\,1.18\%; \S\ref{sec:composability}).

% Section 5 — DocRED Results (compressed, 1450→~600 words)

\subsection{Cross-Dataset Validation on DocRED}
\label{sec:docred-results}

Table~\ref{tab:docred-ablation} presents the four-way ablation on DocRED (96 Wikidata relation types, 14$\times$ SciERC; Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 998 documents).

Best per column in \textbf{bold} (CF excluded; Tot.\ included).

\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
Full S1 reduces DR from 18.46\% to 10.21\% ($\downarrow$45\%), eliminates ET ($\to$\,0\%), and eliminates RV (29.66\%\,$\to$\,0.03\%).\footnote{The residual 0.03\% RV traces to a rare XGrammar automaton edge case where subword tokens from different enum entries combine into chimeric values (e.g., \texttt{member} + \texttt{icipant\_of} from \texttt{member\_of} and \texttt{participant\_of}). This has been reported upstream and is not a fundamental limitation of the approach.}
R-F1 improves from 7.74 to 8.23 ($+$0.50\,pp; $p < 0.001$), attributable to elimination of 5{,}189 OOV relation predictions.
CF increases from 0.10\% to 2.57\%, consistent with the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Residual zero-shot DR (10.21\%) traces to grammar-first fallback under tight constraints ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$; \S\ref{sec:greedy-limitation}); causal tracing confirms all residual DR occurs at fallback positions (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}).

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_grammar_only, phase2_docred_semantic_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET but \emph{increases} DR to 26.17\%: vocabulary restriction makes OOV outputs evaluable, exposing latent type incompatibilities.
Semantic-only reduces DR by 25\% but cannot eliminate RV or ET, the same empirical enabling dependency observed on SciERC.
Residual DR (10.21\% vs.\ 0.93\% on SciERC) reflects high $\bar{\kappa}$ (0.842) and \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity; fine-tuning narrows DR to $\leq$\,0.09\% (Table~\ref{tab:composability}), with the 36 residual violations decomposing into entity type errors (39\%), schema coverage gaps (33\%), incorrect relation selection (17\%), and direction reversal (11\%; Appendix~\ref{app:residual-dr-analysis}).

% All numbers verified against registry 2026-05-14.

\subsection{Ablation and Composability with Fine-Tuning}
\label{sec:scierc-results}

Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} presents the five-way ablation on SciERC (Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 551 documents); only the active constraint layers differ across rows.

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (a) Core result
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: R-F1=0.0823; phase2_scierc_full_s1: R-F1=0.0836
% bootstrap: delta=+0.13pp, CI=[-0.24,+0.58], p=0.5824
Full S1 reduces DR from 15.37\% to 0.93\% ($\downarrow$94\%) while R-F1 is unchanged (8.23\,$\to$\,8.36, $p{=}0.58$).
Per-relation DR drops to $\leq$2.82\%, reaching 0\% on 4/7 relations (Appendix~\ref{app:per-relation-landscape}).
Post-hoc filtering discards up to 48\% of predictions rather than correcting them (Appendix~\ref{app:posthoc-extended}).
Total type-violation burden (Tot.\,=\,DR+CF) decreases from 15.45\% to 10.83\% ($\downarrow$30\%), reflecting \emph{violation conversion}: DR enforcement replaces ontologically invalid triples with individually valid but type-inconsistent ones (CF 0.08\%\,$\to$\,9.90\%); under fine-tuning, Tot.\ drops to 1.18\% with CF\,$\leq$\,1.3\% (Table~\ref{tab:composability}).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (b) Grammar layer
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
% phase2_scierc_grammar_only: RV=0, ET=0, DR=0.1484, R-F1=0.0823
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET with no F1 impact while DR remains at 14.84\%, the ceiling of grammar-based decoding~\cite{geng2023gcd}; grammar-only CF is near-zero (0.08\%), so CF originates from the semantic layer.
Semantic-only reduces DR by only 24\% and cannot eliminate RV or ET; this is the \emph{empirical enabling dependency}: adding the grammar layer yields a further 92\% reduction (11.65\%\,$\to$\,0.93\%).


% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (d) S1 vs S2
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{S1 vs.\ S2.}
S2 achieves comparable DR (0.97\%) but lower R-F1 and CF; we adopt S1.
% phase2_scierc_full_s2: DR=0.0097, R-F1=0.0803, CF=0.0803, triples=1644

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning
%  exp_ids: w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,
%           w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,
%           w5_qwen_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval, w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval,
%           w5_llama_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
\label{sec:composability}
Fine-tuning alone reduces DR to 1--2\% but leaves residual violations (Table~\ref{tab:composability}); adding S1 yields DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% with R-F1 within $\pm$0.6\,pp (removed triples are 97.6--100\% false positives).
% exp_ids: bootstrap_ci_ft_composability.json
Paired bootstrap tests (10{,}000 resamples) confirm that no $\Delta$R-F1 reaches significance after Bonferroni correction for four comparisons (min.\ $p{=}0.014$; 95\% CIs $\subseteq [-0.76, {+}0.22]$\,pp).
CF drops from $+$9.82\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\,pp (fine-tuned; Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}); beam ($k{=}4$) with LoRA eliminates all four violation types on SciERC (R-F1 43.60, 46.18; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

  & \textbf{$\Delta$DR} \\

\caption{Fine-tuning composability: LoRA $\times$ unconstrained vs.\ S1 on SciERC (551 docs) and DocRED (998 dev docs).

\paragraph{Downstream impact.}
\label{sec:downstream-impact}
Among constraint-removed triples, only 0.49\% match gold labels on average (``lucky violations''), confirming $<$0.5\% recall cost; on Llama SciERC all five are recovered via legal type paths (zero churn; Appendix~\ref{app:lucky-violations}).

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The Director is coordinating final revisions of an EMNLP 2026 paper "OntoCoDec" about type-constrained IE via compiled ontology constraints, with a May 25 deadline. This session handled multiple sequential Patch directives:
   - **Page overflow fix**: Recovering from 35→34 pages after Dream-review-driven revisions pushed the Conclusion off page 8
   - **CF bound unification**: Checking all FT CF% values and unifying the bound across the paper (CF≤1.3%)
   - **Trie baseline data update**: Updating R-F1 numbers after violation_checker.py parse failure bug fix (Qwen 42.57→41.16, Llama 41.42→19.95)
   - **Trie baseline narrative strengthening**: Rewriting the constrained baselines paragraph to use R-F1 + parse failure comparison (per Reviewer Report #70), while maintaining 8-page limit

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - OntoCoDec: Two-layer constrained decoding (grammar + semantic) for IE
   - Grammar layer: CFG-based JSON structure + vocabulary membership
   - Semantic layer: Prefix-decidable with state, runtime entity registry
   - DR (Domain/Range) violations vs CF (Cross-Field) violations
   - Violation conversion: DR enforcement converts to CF; fine-tuning resolves
   - Trie-only baseline (GCD-equivalent): vocabulary membership without JSON structural enforcement
   - Parse failure rates: model-dependent (Llama 50.8% vs Qwen 9.1% under trie-only)
   - EMNLP 2026: 8-page main text limit, unlimited references/appendix
   - Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (4 FT settings)

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **section5_runtime.tex** (Most heavily modified this session)
     - Contains runtime overhead, beam search, 70B evaluation, and constrained baselines paragraphs
     - Current state of constrained baselines paragraph (L21-26):
     ```latex
     \paragraph{Comparison with grammar-constrained approaches.}
     \label{sec:constrained-baselines}
     Our grammar-only ablation (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}, row~2) implements the same constraints as GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} and BoostCD~\cite{boostcd2025}: RV/ET$\to$0\% but only 3\% DR reduction vs.\ Full S1's 94\%.
     ```

% Section 5 — DocRED Results (compressed, 1450→~600 words)
% exp_ids: phase2_docred_unconstrained, phase2_docred_grammar_only,
%          phase2_docred_semantic_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
% All numbers verified against registry 2026-05-14.

\subsection{Cross-Dataset Validation on DocRED}
\label{sec:docred-results}

Table~\ref{tab:docred-ablation} presents the four-way ablation on DocRED (96 Wikidata relation types, 14$\times$ SciERC; Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 998 documents).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: DocRED four-way ablation
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.6pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}l rrrrrr rr@{}}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{6}{c}{\textbf{Violation Rates (\%)}}
& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{F1}} \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-7} \cmidrule(l){8-9}
\textbf{Mode}
  & DR\,$\downarrow$ & $\Delta$DR
  & RV\,$\downarrow$ & ET\,$\downarrow$ & CF & Tot.\,$\downarrow$
  & Rel.\,$\uparrow$ & Ent.\,$\uparrow$ \\
\midrule
Unconstrained
  & 18.46 & ---
  & 29.66 & 2.48
  & 0.10  & 18.56
  & 7.74  & 58.15 \\
Grammar
  & 26.17 & $\uparrow$42\%
  & \textbf{0.03} & \textbf{0}
  & 0.07  & 26.24
  & \textbf{8.31}  & \textbf{59.38} \\
Semantic
  & 13.84 & $\downarrow$25\%
  & 29.87 & 4.22
  & 1.05  & 14.89
  & 7.70  & 57.81 \\
Full (S1)
  & \textbf{10.21} & $\downarrow$\textbf{45\%}
  & \textbf{0.03} & \textbf{0}
  & 2.57  & \textbf{12.78}
  & 8.23  & 59.37 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Four-way ablation on DocRED (998 documents, Qwen3-8B, zero-shot).
$\Delta$DR: relative change vs.\ unconstrained.
Tot.\ = DR + CF (total type-violation burden).
Best per column in \textbf{bold} (CF excluded; Tot.\ included).
F1 $\times$100. Bootstrap significance: R-F1 $+$0.50\,pp ($p < 0.001$).
Grammar-only $\uparrow$DR: vocabulary enforcement makes OOV outputs evaluable, exposing latent violations (see text).}
\label{tab:docred-ablation}
\end{table}

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_unconstrained, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
Full S1 reduces DR from 18.46\% to 10.21\% ($\downarrow$45\%), eliminates ET ($\to$\,0\%), and eliminates RV (29.66\%\,$\to$\,0.03\%).\footnote{Residual 0.03\% RV traces to a rare XGrammar automaton edge case (chimeric subword tokens across enum entries); reported upstream.}
R-F1 improves from 7.74 to 8.23 ($+$0.50\,pp; $p < 0.001$), attributable to elimination of 5{,}189 OOV relation predictions.
CF increases from 0.10\% to 2.57\%, consistent with the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Residual zero-shot DR (10.21\%) traces to grammar-first fallback under tight constraints ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$; \S\ref{sec:greedy-limitation}); causal tracing confirms all residual DR occurs at fallback positions (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}).

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_grammar_only, phase2_docred_semantic_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET but \emph{increases} DR to 26.17\%: vocabulary restriction makes OOV outputs evaluable, exposing latent type incompatibilities.
Semantic-only reduces DR by 25\% but cannot eliminate RV or ET, the same empirical enabling dependency observed on SciERC.
Residual DR (10.21\% vs.\ 0.93\% on SciERC) reflects high $\bar{\kappa}$ (0.842) and \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity; fine-tuning narrows DR to $\leq$\,0.09\% (Table~\ref{tab:composability}), with the 36 residual violations decomposing into entity type errors (39\%), schema coverage gaps (33\%), incorrect relation selection (17\%), and direction reversal (11\%; Appendix~\ref{app:residual-dr-analysis}).

% Section 5 — SciERC Results (Draft)
% Data source: Phase 2 SciERC registry experiments
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_grammar_only,
%          phase2_scierc_semantic_only, phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_scierc_full_s2
% All numbers verified against registry 2026-05-14.

\subsection{Ablation and Composability with Fine-Tuning}
\label{sec:scierc-results}

Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} presents the five-way ablation on SciERC (Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 551 documents); only the active constraint layers differ across rows.

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: SciERC five-way ablation
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.6pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}l rrrrrr rr@{}}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{6}{c}{\textbf{Violation Rates (\%)}}
& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{F1}} \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-7} \cmidrule(l){8-9}
\textbf{Mode}
  & DR\,$\downarrow$ & $\Delta$DR
  & RV\,$\downarrow$ & ET\,$\downarrow$ & CF & Tot.\,$\downarrow$
  & Rel.\,$\uparrow$ & Ent.\,$\uparrow$ \\
\midrule
Unconstrained
  & 15.37 & ---
  & 1.39  & 0.40
  & 0.08  & 15.45
  & 8.23  & 31.01 \\
Grammar
  & 14.84 & $\downarrow$3\%
  & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0}
  & 0.08  & 14.92
  & 8.23  & 30.98 \\
Semantic
  & 11.65 & $\downarrow$24\%
  & 1.51  & 0.40
  & 2.71  & 14.36
  & 8.15  & 31.01 \\
Full (S1)
  & \textbf{0.93} & $\downarrow$\textbf{94\%}
  & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0}
  & 9.90  & \textbf{10.83}
  & \textbf{8.36} & 30.98 \\
Full (S2)
  & 0.97  & $\downarrow$94\%
  & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0}
  & 8.03  & \textbf{9.00}
  & 8.03  & \textbf{31.90} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Five-way ablation on SciERC (551 docs, Qwen3-8B, zero-shot).
$\Delta$DR: relative change vs.\ unconstrained.
Tot.\ = DR + CF (total type-violation burden).
Best per column in \textbf{bold} (CF excluded; Tot.\ included).
F1 $\times$100. Bootstrap: 10{,}000 iterations.
CF: same entity assigned conflicting types across triples.
S1 = single-pass (\S\ref{sec:strategies}), S2 = two-pass (\S\ref{sec:s2}).
Grammar-only represents the ceiling of grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{geng2023gcd}: vocabulary membership is enforced but cross-field semantic constraints are not.}
\label{tab:scierc-ablation}
\end{table}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (a) Core result
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: R-F1=0.0823; phase2_scierc_full_s1: R-F1=0.0836
% bootstrap: delta=+0.13pp, CI=[-0.24,+0.58], p=0.5824
Full S1 reduces DR from 15.37\% to 0.93\% ($\downarrow$94\%) while R-F1 is unchanged (8.23\,$\to$\,8.36, $p{=}0.58$).
Per-relation DR drops to $\leq$2.82\%, reaching 0\% on 4/7 relations (Appendix~\ref{app:per-relation-landscape}).
Post-hoc filtering discards up to 48\% of predictions rather than correcting them (Appendix~\ref{app:posthoc-extended}).
Total type-violation burden (Tot.\,=\,DR+CF) decreases from 15.45\% to 10.83\% ($\downarrow$30\%), reflecting \emph{violation conversion}: DR enforcement replaces ontologically invalid triples with individually valid but type-inconsistent ones (CF 0.08\%\,$\to$\,9.90\%); under fine-tuning, Tot.\ drops to 1.18\% with CF\,$\leq$\,1.3\% (Table~\ref{tab:composability}).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (b) Grammar layer
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
% phase2_scierc_grammar_only: RV=0, ET=0, DR=0.1484, R-F1=0.0823
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET with no F1 impact while DR remains at 14.84\%, the ceiling of grammar-based decoding~\cite{geng2023gcd}; grammar-only CF is near-zero (0.08\%), so CF originates from the semantic layer.
Semantic-only reduces DR by only 24\% and cannot eliminate RV or ET; this is the \emph{empirical enabling dependency}: adding the grammar layer yields a further 92\% reduction (11.65\%\,$\to$\,0.93\%).


% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (d) S1 vs S2
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{S1 vs.\ S2.}
S2 achieves comparable DR (0.97\%) but lower R-F1 and CF; we adopt S1.
% phase2_scierc_full_s2: DR=0.0097, R-F1=0.0803, CF=0.0803, triples=1644

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning
%  exp_ids: w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,
%           w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,
%           w5_qwen_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval, w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval,
%           w5_llama_docred_lora_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
\label{sec:composability}
% exp_ids: bootstrap_ci_ft_composability.json
Fine-tuning alone reduces DR to 1--2\% but leaves residual violations (Table~\ref{tab:composability}); adding S1 yields DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% with no significant $\Delta$R-F1 after Bonferroni correction (min.\ $p{=}0.014$; 95\% CIs $\subseteq [-0.76, {+}0.22]$\,pp; removed triples are 97.6--100\% false positives).
CF drops from $+$9.82\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\,pp (fine-tuned; Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}); beam ($k{=}4$) with LoRA eliminates all four violation types on SciERC (R-F1 43.60, 46.18; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rrrr r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Dataset} & \textbf{Mode}
  & \textbf{DR\,$\downarrow$} & \textbf{CF}
  & \textbf{R-F1\,$\uparrow$} & \textbf{E-F1\,$\uparrow$}
  & \textbf{$\Delta$DR} \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{Qwen3-8B}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{SciERC}
    & Unconstr.\ &  1.95 & 0    & 43.86 & 67.05 & --- \\
  & & Full S1    & \textbf{0} & 1.18 & 43.77 & 67.05 & $\downarrow$100\% \\
\cmidrule(l){2-8}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{DocRED}
    & Unconstr.\ &  0.56 & 0.08 & 40.89 & 82.35 & --- \\
  & & Full S1    & \textbf{0.00} & 0.22 & 40.79 & 81.87 & $\downarrow$100\% \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{\shortstack[l]{Llama\\3.1-8B}}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{SciERC}
    & Unconstr.\ &  1.11 & 0    & 45.45 & 67.76 & --- \\
  & & Full S1    &  0.09 & 0.46 & 45.47 & 67.76 & $\downarrow$92\% \\
\cmidrule(l){2-8}
  & \multirow{2}{*}{DocRED}
    & Unconstr.\ &  0.49 & 0.08 & 44.55 & 84.77 & --- \\
  & & Full S1    &  0.00 & 0.26 & 44.70 & 84.71 & $\downarrow$100\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Fine-tuning composability: LoRA $\times$ unconstrained vs.\ S1 on SciERC (551 docs) and DocRED (998 dev docs).
F1\,$\times$100.
Paired bootstrap (B${=}$10{,}000, document-level): no $\Delta$R-F1 reaches significance after Bonferroni correction ($\alpha/4{=}0.0125$; min.\ $p{=}0.014$; all 95\% CIs $\subseteq [-0.76, {+}0.22]$\,pp); DR reduction is significant in all settings ($p{<}0.001$).
E-F1 includes parse-failure documents (Qwen PF: 7--8\%; Llama PF: 2--3\%).}
\label{tab:composability}
\end{table}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (f) Downstream impact of DR elimination
%  exp_ids: task_e_lucky_violation_analysis
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Downstream impact.}
\label{sec:downstream-impact}
Among constraint-removed triples, only 0.49\% match gold labels on average (``lucky violations''), confirming $<$0.5\% recall cost; on Llama SciERC all five are recovered via legal type paths (zero churn; Appendix~\ref{app:lucky-violations}).

1	\section{Related Work}
2	\label{sec:related_work}
3	
4	We provide a detailed survey in Appendix~\ref{app:related_work}; here we position OntoCoDec along three axes.
5	
6	\paragraph{Constrained decoding.}
7	XGrammar~\cite{dong2025xgrammar}, Outlines~\cite{willard2023outlines}, SynCode~\cite{ugare2024syncode}, and related systems~\cite{beurer-kellner2023lmql,park2024grammar,jsonschemabench2025} enforce format validity via CFG-based token masking.
8	NeuroLogic Decoding~\cite{lu2021neurologic} enforces predicate-logic constraints via beam-level reranking; OntoCoDec applies constraints per-token via forward masking, avoiding beam-width dependence.
9	In code generation, PICARD~\cite{scholak2021picard} and \citet{pldi2025_type_constrained_codegen} compile type systems into prefix automata, but IE type environments accumulate dynamically (\S\ref{sec:composition}).
10	
11	\paragraph{Schema-aware IE.}
12	GoLLIE~\cite{sainz2024gollie}, KnowCoder~\cite{knowcoder_acl2024}, GUIDEX~\cite{guidex2025}, GenIE~\cite{josifoski2022genie}, TANL~\cite{paolini2021tanl}, REBEL~\cite{cabot2021rebel}, InstructUIE~\cite{wang2023instructuie}, and others~\cite{fei2022lasuie,wang2022deepstruct,lu2022uie,lou2023usm,zhou2024universalner} encode ontology structure or frame IE as structured generation, though schema compliance gaps persist~\cite{wadhwa2023revisiting}.
13	GoLLIE and KnowCoder embed schema knowledge via code-style prompts, achieving structural compliance without runtime enforcement; GoLLIE-7B eliminates DR via its dataclass format but at severe coverage cost (R-F1${=}$0.0, 46\% empty output), while OntoCoDec with LoRA achieves R-F1${=}$45.47 at DR${=}$0.09\%, surpassing KnowCoder-7B (supervised R-F1${=}$40.0)~\cite{knowcoder_acl2024}.
14	The paradigms are complementary: GoLLIE constrains output format, OntoCoDec constrains content generation.
15	
16	\paragraph{Constraint enforcement in IE.}
17	\citet{roth_yih_2004} and \citet{riedel2010modeling} formulated hard type constraints via ILP; post-hoc validation~\cite{khorshidi2025odke,spires_2024,ontologx_2025} detects violations after generation but discards up to 48\% of predictions including true positives.
18	EnriCo~\cite{zaratiana2024enrico} uses ASP; IterGen~\cite{ugare2025itergen} backtracks on violations---OntoCoDec uses forward-only masking at $O(|V|)$ per step, avoiding backtracking latency.
19	Grammar-only enforcement (GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd}, BoostCD~\cite{boostcd2025}) achieves only 3\% DR reduction (\S\ref{sec:constrained-baselines}); DCCD~\cite{dccd2026} explores draft-conditioned constrained decoding.
20	Extraction tasks are robust to format constraints~\cite{tam2024letmespeak} despite degradation in other domains~\cite{banerjee2025crane,formattax2026}.
21

63	R-F1 improves from 7.74 to 8.23 ($+$0.50\,pp; $p < 0.001$), attributable to elimination of 5{,}189 OOV relation predictions.
64	CF increases from 0.10\% to 2.57\%, consistent with the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
65	Residual zero-shot DR (10.21\%) traces to grammar-first fallback under tight constraints ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$; \S\ref{sec:greedy-limitation}); causal tracing confirms all residual DR occurs at fallback positions (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}).

\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
Full S1 reduces DR from 18.46\% to 10.21\% ($\downarrow$45\%), eliminates ET ($\to$\,0\%), and eliminates RV (29.66\%\,$\to$\,0.03\%).\footnote{Residual 0.03\% RV traces to a rare XGrammar automaton edge case (chimeric subword tokens across enum entries); reported upstream.}
R-F1 improves from 7.74 to 8.23 ($+$0.50\,pp; $p < 0.001$), attributable to elimination of 5{,}189 OOV relation predictions.
CF increases from 0.10\% to 2.57\%, consistent with the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Residual zero-shot DR (10.21\%) traces to grammar-first fallback under tight constraints ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$; \S\ref{sec:greedy-limitation}); causal tracing confirms all residual DR occurs at fallback positions (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}).

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_grammar_only, phase2_docred_semantic_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET but \emph{increases} DR to 26.17\%: vocabulary restriction makes OOV outputs evaluable, exposing latent type incompatibilities.
Semantic-only reduces DR by 25\% but cannot eliminate RV or ET, the same empirical enabling dependency observed on SciERC.
Residual DR (10.21\% vs.\ 0.93\% on SciERC) reflects high $\bar{\kappa}$ (0.842) and \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity; fine-tuning narrows DR to $\leq$\,0.09\% (Table~\ref{tab:composability}), with the 36 residual violations decomposing into entity type errors (39\%), schema coverage gaps (33\%), incorrect relation selection (17\%), and direction reversal (11\%; Appendix~\ref{app:residual-dr-analysis}).

% All numbers verified against registry 2026-05-14.

\subsection{Ablation and Composability with Fine-Tuning}
\label{sec:scierc-results}

Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} presents the five-way ablation on SciERC (Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 551 documents); only the active constraint layers differ across rows.

%  (a) Core result
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: R-F1=0.0823; phase2_scierc_full_s1: R-F1=0.0836
% bootstrap: delta=+0.13pp, CI=[-0.24,+0.58], p=0.5824
Full S1 reduces DR from 15.37\% to 0.93\% ($\downarrow$94\%) while R-F1 is unchanged (8.23\,$\to$\,8.36, $p{=}0.58$).
Per-relation DR drops to $\leq$2.82\%, reaching 0\% on 4/7 relations (Appendix~\ref{app:per-relation-landscape}).
Post-hoc filtering discards up to 48\% of predictions rather than correcting them (Appendix~\ref{app:posthoc-extended}).
Total type-violation burden (Tot.\,=\,DR+CF) decreases from 15.45\% to 10.83\% ($\downarrow$30\%), reflecting \emph{violation conversion}: DR enforcement replaces ontologically invalid triples with individually valid but type-inconsistent ones (CF 0.08\%\,$\to$\,9.90\%); under fine-tuning, Tot.\ drops to 1.18\% with CF\,$\leq$\,1.3\% (Table~\ref{tab:composability}).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (b) Grammar layer
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
% phase2_scierc_grammar_only: RV=0, ET=0, DR=0.1484, R-F1=0.0823
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET with no F1 impact while DR remains at 14.84\%, the ceiling of grammar-based decoding~\cite{geng2023gcd}; grammar-only CF is near-zero (0.08\%), so CF originates from the semantic layer.
Semantic-only reduces DR by only 24\% and cannot eliminate RV or ET; this is the \emph{empirical enabling dependency}: adding the grammar layer yields a further 92\% reduction (11.65\%\,$\to$\,0.93\%).


% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  (d) S1 vs S2
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\paragraph{S1 vs.\ S2.}
S2 achieves comparable DR (0.97\%) but lower R-F1 and CF; we adopt S1.

CF drops from $+$9.82\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\,pp (fine-tuned; Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}); beam ($k{=}4$) with LoRA eliminates all four violation types on SciERC (R-F1 43.60, 46.18; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_unconstrained, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
Full S1 reduces DR from 18.46\% to 10.21\% ($\downarrow$45\%), eliminates ET ($\to$\,0\%), and eliminates RV (29.66\%\,$\to$\,0.03\%).\footnote{Residual 0.03\% RV traces to a rare XGrammar automaton edge case (chimeric subword tokens across enum entries); reported upstream.}
R-F1 improves from 7.74 to 8.23 ($+$0.50\,pp; $p < 0.001$), attributable to elimination of 5{,}189 OOV relation predictions.
CF increases from 0.10\% to 2.57\%, consistent with the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Residual zero-shot DR (10.21\%) traces to grammar-first fallback under tight constraints ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$; \S\ref{sec:greedy-limitation}); causal tracing confirms all residual DR occurs at fallback positions (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}).

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_grammar_only, phase2_docred_semantic_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET but \emph{increases} DR to 26.17\%: vocabulary restriction makes OOV outputs evaluable, exposing latent type incompatibilities.
Semantic-only reduces DR by 25\% but cannot eliminate RV or ET, the same empirical enabling dependency observed on SciERC.
Residual DR (10.21\% vs.\ 0.93\% on SciERC) reflects high $\bar{\kappa}$ (0.842) and \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity; fine-tuning narrows DR to $\leq$\,0.09\% (Table~\ref{tab:composability}), with the 36 residual violations decomposing into entity type errors (39\%), schema coverage gaps (33\%), incorrect relation selection (17\%), and direction reversal (11\%; Appendix~\ref{app:residual-dr-analysis}).

toolUseResult.newString:
Entity F1 impact is model-dependent ($+$1.22\,pp for Qwen vs.\ $-$0.64\,pp for Llama on DocRED), partially confounded by increased parse failures under constraints (Llama: 9.1\% vs.\ 6.8\%).
On 70B DocRED LoRA, parse failure rises modestly under S1 (10.0\%\,$\to$\,12.5\%) due to generation timeouts on long documents rather than JSON format errors; SciERC (shorter documents) shows 0\% parse failure in both settings.

lines: Global entity-level type consensus during decoding offers the most direct path to resolving CF violations.

CF type inconsistencies may propagate to downstream tasks that consume extracted triples (e.g., knowledge graph construction, question answering); the impact of such propagation has not been evaluated.
Entity F1 impact is model-dependent ($+$1.22\,pp for Qwen vs.\ $-$0.64\,pp for Llama on DocRED), partially confounded by increased parse failures under constraints (Llama: 9.1\% vs.\ 6.8\%).

+On 70B DocRED LoRA, parse failure rises modestly under S1 (10.0\%\,$\to$\,12.5\%) due to generation timeouts on long documents rather than JSON format errors; SciERC (shorter documents) shows 0\% parse failure in both settings.

Residual DR under fine-tuning (36 violations across all fine-tuned settings, both models and both datasets) decomposes into entity type errors (39\%), schema coverage gaps (33\%), and model generation errors correctly caught by constraints (28\%); Llama DocRED alone accounts for 33 of 36 residual violations (92\%), reflecting weaker entity typing (Appendix~\ref{app:residual-dr-analysis}).

Schema coverage gaps (one-third of residual violations) arise because RE constraints are extracted from training-data type pairs, which may not cover all valid combinations; larger training sets or manual constraint table completion can reduce this gap.
